predictions.title: Reward reinvestment is vulnerable to spot-price sandwich manipulation
predictions.description: RewardReinvestor sends withdrawn reward tokens through IDexHandler.buyMalt(), while UniswapHandler.buyMalt() performs a router swap with amountOutMin set to zero. An attacker can front-run a public reinvestment transaction, temporarily skew the reward/Malt pool reserves, allow the reinvestor to execute at a severely unfavorable spot price, and then back-run to restore the pool. Because no minimum Malt output is enforced, the transaction can succeed while converting the user's rewards into materially less Malt than expected.
predictions.impact: A user can lose most of the economic value of withdrawn rewards while receiving and bonding an attacker-manipulated, substantially smaller Malt amount; the attacker captures the difference through sandwich arbitrage.
predictions.mitigation: Require the reinvestment caller to supply a minimum acceptable Malt output and deadline, propagate that bound into the router swap, and revert when it is not met. Prefer a manipulation-resistant TWAP or oracle-derived bound for any system-level validation, and avoid calculating protection solely from the current pool reserves.
